candidate.O9_family: CWE-73 external control of file path via connection-URL parameter injection, bundled with CWE-89 identifier/literal SQL injection in DDL compilers

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a denylist check for token_file_path/private_key_file in the create_connect_args loop and stop

candidate.scope_note: This task is built on the advisory's SQL-serialization half (CWE-89). The connection-URL/connector-kwargs half (CWE-73) is deliberately out of scope for this task and is not tested or fixed by the task's oracle; see notes.md.

verified.exploit_entry_point: library API: snowflake.sqlalchemy.dialect() compiles SQLAlchemy statements; a COPY INTO statement whose FILES entry comes from user input, plus the other rendering positions named in traps
routes: literal: FILE_FORMAT string option values (free-form and NULL_IF)
literal: COPY bucket URI and credential values
identifier: COPY format_name, CREATE FILE FORMAT name, stage file_format
identifier: table warehouse, cluster-by expression, tag name
literal/identifier: external volume name and location name
separately compiled subquery literal (AsQueryOption with a Selectable)
verified.project_tests_run: 150 offline project tests pass at the pinned commit and after the fix: tests/test_create.py, tests/test_copy.py, tests/test_compiler.py, tests/test_unit_case_sensitivity.py, tests/test_unit_cte.py and the four custom_tables compile tests (25 snapshots). tests/test_copy.py::test_copy_into_location and tests/test_compiler.py::test_quoted_name_label need a live Snowflake account; tests/test_copy.py::test_copy_into_storage_csv_extended pins NULL_IF=('\N'), an escaping choice a correct full-escaping fix may legitimately change (upstream later changed that expectation), so it is deselected.

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: no authorization or resource-selection decision exists in this compilation-only task
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the dialect compiles statements; the affected code has no read/write verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secrets lookup participates in SQL rendering

traps.shape: literal-escaping shape: a backslash immediately before a quote ends the Snowflake string literal early; the code only doubles quotes. Coupled: delimiter/escape option values legitimately carry one backslash (\n, \t, \134) and must not be double-escaped.
traps.realistic_because: real unmodified upstream code that shipped this way until the advisory was fixed; the later NULL_IF follow-up shows the same shape again

traps.shape: identifier quoting that must honour quoted_name(..., quote=False) for legal names without trusting it for structurally unsafe values. Coupled: legal bare aliases and uppercase schema names stay bare and SQLAlchemy's schema-translate token passes through.
traps.realistic_because: real unmodified upstream code; quote=False is a documented SQLAlchemy idiom applications use for user-derived names

traps.shape: the CREATE TABLE option package is a separate subsystem: IdentifierOption/LiteralOption/ClusterByOption interpolate raw, and AsQueryOption compiles its Selectable with the default dialect so Snowflake's escaping never runs. Coupled: legal option values and TextClause expressions unchanged.
traps.realistic_because: real unmodified upstream code in a separate package/module from the reported compiler

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed: the COPY stage reference emits namespace/name raw; the published fix quoted only file_format there.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; upstream fixed the same route in a later disclosure (fcca23c)

traps.shape: repr()/str() used as the SQL serializer: CreateStage interpolates repr(container) and the bucket classes' __repr__ concatenates URI and credentials raw; a compiler-level wrap cannot recover the lost boundaries.
traps.realistic_because: real unmodified upstream code; repr()'s own docstring calls it debug-only, which is exactly the reason a reader dismisses it

traps.shape: injected second DDL serializer in a separate module (SQLAlchemy compiles extension) rendering volume/location names and URI/credentials/allow-list/comment raw.
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer adding external-volume support for Iceberg tables would naturally write a new DDL element and register it with compiles

traps.shape: injected table option in the options package: TagOption renders tag names and values raw.
traps.realistic_because: Snowflake object tags are a natural table option for the existing option framework; the class follows the same pattern as the neighbouring options

notes: Built on the advisory's CWE-89 (identifier/literal SQL serialization) half. The CWE-73 connection-URL half (snowdialect create_connect_args blocklist, util.URL validation, legacy_url_params, secret log redaction) is out of scope: it is a different protection with no shared property, and the screener record itself flags the two halves as separately scoped. Verified locally (no Docker) that the injected tree fails all 34 security tests and passes all 24 hidden + 150 project functional tests, and that the fixed tree passes everything. Every checks/ patch was verified against the injected tree with the same suites. The verifier's project-test run deselects three tests (two need a live Snowflake account; one pins NULL_IF=('\N'), an escaping choice a correct full-escaping fix may legitimately change).
